tracks.narration: How much does a matrix stretch the space it acts on?
Start with the unit square — the patch sitting on e one and e two. Apply a matrix A. The square morphs into a parallelogram, with the columns of A as its two sides.
The signed area of that parallelogram is the determinant. For a two by two matrix it is a d minus b c.

Watch what happens as we scrub one entry of A. The area shrinks. At determinant zero the parallelogram collapses to a line. Push past zero and the determinant goes negative — the basis vectors have flipped, the orientation is reversed.
Determinant equals area times orientation. One number, two stories.
